{{short description|Conjecture about the roots of polynomials}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Sendov's theorem''' (formally a conjecture), sometimes also called '''Ilieff's conjecture''', concerns the relationship between the locations of [[root of a polynomial|roots]] and [[critical point (mathematics)|critical point]]s of a [[polynomial function]] of a [[complex variable]].  It is named after [[Blagovest Sendov]].

The [[conjecture]] states that for a polynomial

: <math> f(z) = (z - r_1)\cdots (z-r_n),\quad n\ge 2, </math>

with all roots ''r''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''r''<sub>''n''</sub> inside the [[closed unit disk]], each of the ''n'' roots is at a distance no more than&nbsp;1 from at least one [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical point]].

The [[Gauss–Lucas theorem]] says that all of the critical points lie within the [[convex hull]] of the roots.  It follows that the critical points must be within the unit disk, since the roots are.

The conjecture was previously [[mathematical proof|proven]] for&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;<&nbsp;9 by Brown and Xiang and for&nbsp;''n'' [[Eventually (mathematics)|sufficiently large]] by [[Terence Tao|Tao]].<ref name="Tao2020arxiv">{{cite arXiv |eprint=2012.04125 |author=Terence Tao |title=Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials|year=2020 |class=math.CV }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|author=Terence Tao|website=What's new|url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2020/12/08/sendovs-conjecture-for-sufficiently-high-degree-polynomials/|title=Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials |date=9 December 2020}}</ref>

There is also a generalisation by Dean Phelps and Rene S. Rodriguez: {{zbl|id=0244.30001}}

On 5 August 2026, a proof of Sendov's conjecture generated using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Pro was posted by Lech Mazur.<ref name="Mazur2026">{{cite web |last=Mazur |first=Lech |date=5 August 2026 |title=A proof of Sendov's conjecture |url=https://www.proofatlas.ai/papers/sendov-conjecture/SENDOV_CONJECTURE_PROOF_AUGUST_5_2026.pdf |website=ProofAtlas |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref> [[Terence Tao]] subsequently published an exposition verifying and simplifying the argument, and extended the method to resolve the Phelps–Rodriguez conjecture.<ref name="Tao2026">{{cite web |last=Tao |first=Terence |date=12 August 2026 |title=A digestion of the proof of Sendov's conjecture |url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/08/12/a-digestion-of-the-proof-of-sendovs-conjecture/ |website=What's new |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref><ref name="Alexeev2026">{{cite web |last=Alexeev |first=Boris |title=Lean 4 formalization of Sendov's conjecture |url=https://github.com/BorisAlexeev/sendov |year=2026 |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>

==History==
{{more citations needed|date=July 2015}}

The conjecture was first proposed by [[Blagovest Sendov]] in 1959; he described the conjecture to his colleague [[Nikola Obreshkov]]. In 1967 the conjecture was misattributed<ref>Marden, Morris. Conjectures on the Critical Points of a Polynomial. [[The American Mathematical Monthly]] 90 (1983), no. 4, 267-276.</ref> to Ljubomir Iliev by [[Walter Hayman]].<ref>Problem 4.5, W. K. Hayman, Research Problems in Function Theory. Althlone Press, London, 1967.</ref> In 1969 Meir and Sharma proved the conjecture for polynomials with ''n'' < 6. In 1991 Brown proved the conjecture for ''n'' < 7. Borcea extended the proof to ''n'' < 8 in 1996. Brown and Xiang<ref>Brown, Johnny E.; Xiang, Guangping Proof of the Sendov conjecture for polynomials of degree at most eight. [[Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications]] 232 (1999), no. 2, 272–292.</ref> proved the conjecture for ''n'' < 9 in 1999. In 2020, [[Terence Tao]] proved the conjecture  in the special case of polynomials with sufficiently high [[Degree of a polynomial|degree]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Tao | first1=Terence 
| title=Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials
| date=2022
| arxiv=2012.04125
| journal=Acta Mathematica
| volume=229
| issue=2
| pages=347–392
| doi=10.4310/ACTA.2022.v229.n2.a3 | doi-access=free}}</ref>
